Murshid is an AI-powered intelligent academic advising platform designed to improve the university experience through advanced multi-agent AI technologies. The system automatically answers student inquiries, tracks academic progress, calculates GPA and completed hours, and identifies recommended courses in real time.
The project integrates Artificial Intelligence, Web Technologies, and Cloud Infrastructure to create a complete academic advising solution. Murshid utilizes the massive context window of the
and a unique multi-agent architecture (including Data and Reroute agents) to provide natural, accurate, and on-topic advising while maintaining high-speed inference over the internet.

The target users of the system include university students, academic advisors (doctors), and university administration. The success of the project will be measured through the detection accuracy of the AI, the speed of retrieving student data, and the reduction of repetitive queries directed at human advisors.

Universities currently suffer from significant bottlenecks during registration periods due to a high volume of repetitive student inquiries. By automating these interactions, universities can significantly optimize faculty time and improve student satisfaction, leading to better academic outcomes and smoother operations.
In the traditional academic advising system, several inefficiencies negatively impact both students and faculty:

University doctors and academic advisors spend a significant amount of their valuable time answering the exact same routine questions from hundreds of students (e.g., registration dates, prerequisite inquiries, and graduation requirements).
Because advisors are bogged down by these repetitive questions, they have less time to provide real, in-depth support to students who are facing complex academic or personal challenges that

Human advisors are only available during specific office hours, leaving students without immediate guidance when they are planning their schedules or making urgent academic decisions late at night or on weekends.

4.4 Self-Hosted LLM vs. Commercial APIs (ChatGPT / Gemini)
A fundamental architectural decision for Murshid was choosing to self-host the Qwen 3.6:35B model on a dedicated
server rather than simply relying on commercial APIs like OpenAI's ChatGPT or Google's Gemini. This decision was driven by three main factors:

Commercial APIs require sending potentially sensitive university and student data to third-party servers. By self-hosting the LLM, we ensure that all student queries and academic data remain strictly within the

Commercial APIs are "black boxes" with strict, unchangeable guardrails. Self-hosting gives us full root-level access to modify the model's parameters, tweak inference configurations (like temperature and repetition penalties), and implement custom system prompts exactly how we want.
While connecting to a ChatGPT API takes only a few lines of code, successfully hosting a massive 35

parameter LLM locally is an extremely difficult engineering feat. It requires deep knowledge of GPU memory constraints (which is why 8-bit quantization was utilized), managing server load for concurrent users, and handling complex Linux/CUDA server maintenance. Taking on this challenging approach demonstrates a much higher level of engineering competence for this graduation project.
strictly adheres to university guidelines, we built a highly optimized, multi-agent architecture rather than relying on a single prompt:

Before the main model answers, a Data Agent searches and retrieves the most relevant university data, feeding the best-fit information to the main model to ensure high accuracy and fast data retrieval.
A specialized agent continuously monitors the conversation. If a student tries to change the subject or go
, the Reroute Agent ensures the AI seamlessly changes the topic within the app use case and prevents it from hallucinating.

We crafted highly detailed system prompts so that the model consistently delivers excellent, natural-sounding responses, regardless of whether the student types a well-structured question or a poorly phrased one.

Building a production-ready AI platform from scratch presented several major challenges that we successfully overcame:

The toughest challenge was optimizing the prompts to ensure the model acted naturally while strictly preventing it from "hallucinating" or answering questions outside the provided university data. We solved this through the multi-agent system described above.
We wanted the project to be easily accessible over the internet rather than just running locally. We successfully purchased a domain name and configured
to host the project, ensuring a reliable, public-facing web infrastructure.
Transitioning the database from a local environment to a live, secure Google Cloud SQL instance required careful configuration of environment variables to maintain stable, persistent connections.
Ensuring the user interface looked perfect and did not break when switching between English and Arabic required rewriting the styling using modern CSS logical properties.

Integrating the Resend email system to securely deliver One-Time Passwords (OTPs) while enforcing that only students with verified university emails could register required complex backend validation logic.

The Murshid platform successfully demonstrates how modern AI can be practically applied within an educational institution. By handling routine inquiries, Murshid not only provides students with immediate, accurate, and personalized academic guidance, but it also restores valuable time to university doctors, allowing them to focus on meaningful mentorship and complex student needs.
